subject: HIPAA intake: BAA pathways, PHI scope, and deployment eligibility
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Kate Morrison <kate.morrison@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: HIPAA intake recap + next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Kate — it was helpful to walk through HealthLytics' use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

1) PHI scope (as discussed)
- Primary PHI types: patient identifiers, encounter metadata, clinical notes extraction (NLP output may contain identifiers)
- Source systems: EHR exports (S3), occasional CSV uploads from downstream analytics

2) Desired deployments for PHI workloads
- Preferred: Private deployment (VPC + customer-managed network) — HealthLytics asked for on-prem adjacency
- Secondary: Dedicated capacity in a private tenant (reserved GPUs) with encrypted storage
- Not acceptable: Public hosted multi-tenant endpoints for PHI (we agreed)

3) Compliance and legal
- You asked whether Redwood provides a BAA: yes, we can execute a BAA for eligible deployment modes (private or dedicated with contractual controls) — we will share our standard BAA draft for review.
- SOC 2: Redwood is Type II in progress (SOC 2 Type II audit Q2 2025 completed for infra controls; full-report package available on request once we finish internal redaction)

4) Evidence & questionnaire
- Please send the vendor security questionnaire you prefer (SSQ or custom). We'll centralize responses and provide supporting evidence where applicable.

5) Next steps I recommend:
- Kate to share vendor security questionnaire and expected list of evidence by EOD 1/12
- HealthLytics to confirm preferred deployment option (Private VPC vs Dedicated) and typical daily volume of PHI records
- Redwood to share: HIPAA intake form (attached), draft BAA, and a short checklist of evidence items

Attachments: redwood-hipaa-intake-form.pdf, BAA-template-Redwood-Draft.docx (draft)

Happy to hop on a follow-up call if it helps — Monica (cc) will own the technical intake with Dev.

—
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.com

From: Kate Morrison <kate.morrison@healthlytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthLytics Security <security@healthlytics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jan 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: HIPAA intake recap + next steps

Thanks Jasmine — this is great, appreciated. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We will push our vendor security questionnaire to you by EOD Monday 1/12. It's a 52-question PDF (we use a slightly modified SIG-lite).
- Deployment: HealthLytics' security leadership prefers Private VPC for any workload touching PHI. Dedicated (single-tenant) reserved capacity is an acceptable alternative if private VPC is not viable, but we need the guarantee that data does not traverse shared-model endpoints.
- On SOC 2: we'll need the SOC 2 report and related controls matrix; we can accept redacted reports for now. Please indicate when we can expect the artifact.

One question: Do you offer key management integrations (KMS/HSM) where we can bring our own keys? That is a gating control for our security team.

Attaching: HealthLytics-vendor-security-questionnaire.pdf (preliminary)

—
Kate Morrison
Director, Product Security
HealthLytics
kate.morrison@healthlytics.com
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: HealthLytics Security <security@healthlytics.com>, Kate Morrison <kate.morrison@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: HIPAA intake recap + next steps

Hi Kate / security team — looping in a few technical constraints and what we can provide today versus via roadmap: 

Summary (short):
- Eligible PHI workflows: Private VPC deployment (control plane isolated, customer-managed networking) and Redwood Private On-Prem package are fully supported for PHI. Dedicated reserved capacity can be scoped to customer-only tenancy and encrypted volumes. Public hosted endpoints are not eligible for PHI.

Technical details and asks: 
- KMS/BYOK: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations for both Private VPC and Dedicated (AWS KMS/Customer key policies). HSM-based BYOK is supported on a case-by-case basis; we'll need to scope the HSM integration in the security questionnaire.
- Data-in-transit & at-rest: TLS 1.2+ for transit; at-rest encryption with customer-managed keys (when configured).
- Data residency: For Private deployments we can pin region (us-east-1 / us-west-2). Dedicated reservations can also be region-specific.
- Logging & audit: We can provide audit logs (API-level, model invocation metadata) and long-term retention as an add-on. Please specify retention window required.

Please find attached a simple example data-flow diagram showing where PHI could flow in a Private VPC setup (example-data-flow-diagram.png).

Questions for HealthLytics to answer in the questionnaire:
- Typical payload sizes and whether you will submit full EHR dumps or incremental deltas
- Expected PII/PHI fields: will you send explicit identifiers (SSNs, MRNs) or rely on pseudonymization upstream?
- Required retention window for audit logs and model outputs

If you want, Monica and I can schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive to validate the network controls and KMS configuration.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

Kate — thanks for the quick turnaround and the questionnaire. Next steps from Redwoods' side: 

- I'll run through the questionnaire and populate answers where we can; expect an initial pass by EOD Wed 1/14.
- Jasmine will send the BAA draft link for your legal team to review: https://docusign.redwood.example/BAA-HL-3247 (attached as a draft).
- Action item for HealthLytics: confirm preferred deployment (Private VPC or Dedicated) and provide sample payload (redacted) if possible so we can validate tokenization/pseudonymization expectations.
- We'll include a short checklist of evidence items you can expect (SOC artifact, architecture diagrams, key management config, data flow diagram).

If it helps, propose a 30-min technical sync Thursday 1/15 at 10:00am PT to cover KMS and network boundaries. Reply with a calendar invite if that works.
